entries.question: Where does hn serve enforce the push verdict, and how are protected updates serialized?
entries.rationale: pre-receive sees quarantined objects and a non-zero exit rejects every ref and discards the pushed objects (FR-012), verified by spike with git 2.53. Hooks cannot hold a lock across the ref update, so the wrapper takes a flock before starting receive-pack and shares the descriptor with it. Every check and ref update for one hosted repository then runs one push at a time (FR-022, NFR-005). post-receive records branch owners and the push log only after refs move. proc-receive and reference-transaction were rejected because they require reimplementing ref updates or split non-atomic pushes into separate transactions.

Without --remote, hn merge keeps its --no-ff path unchanged (FR-016). Existing merge-fact validation binds only subject, head, policy and evidence, so commit=head validates without a protocol change.

entries.question: How does the push check reuse replication validation without duplicating it?
entries.rationale: Reuse satisfies FR-007 literally. The exception is required because hn sync publishes actor refs before proposal refs in separate pushes; without it, the actor push would need the proposal ref and the proposal ref would need the candidate, so neither could land. Range validation and the batched reader keep NFR-001 within 5 seconds at 1,000 events; per-commit git show of every hosted event would cost about 2,000 subprocesses.

entries.rationale: Maintainers sign decisions against the base policy digest, so filtering by the destination digest would discard every acceptance whenever the policy changed. Applying destination actor lists and thresholds to the same signed facts implements C-004 and the edge case that evidence from actors removed from the destination policy does not count. Re-signing would change the wire format and the existing governance flow.

Imported branches have no owner. Hubnot facts arrive afterwards through governed pushes such as hn sync. Recovery of a protected tip with invalid policy is a documented administrator procedure: run git update-ref as the server user while holding the repository lock through hn serve repo lock-exec NAME -- COMMAND.

entries.question: What does hn serve repo create import, what must hold at creation, and how does an administrator recover a protected branch with no valid policy (OQ-11)?
entries.rationale: Mirroring refs/hn/* would host facts that never passed FR-007 or FR-010, which breaks the FR-017 claim that every advertised fact was validated on arrival. A protected branch without valid policy can never move through the governed path, so creating one only produces a dead repository; refusing at creation is fail-closed and gives a clear message. lock-exec gives administrators the repository lock without adding a governed-path bypass.

entries.final_answer: Implement the git-lfs-transfer SSH protocol (version 1: batch, put-object, verify-object, get-object; every lock command answers unsupported) with the standard library. git-lfs-authenticate is refused as unsupported-command. Objects live at state/repos/NAME/lfs/objects/OID[0:2]/OID[2:4]/OID; uploads stream into state/repos/NAME/lfs/incoming, are checked for size and SHA-256, and are renamed into place only while holding the repository LFS lock, after a quota recheck. The quota counts verified stored bytes only.
options: git-lfs-transfer pure SSH protocol only, objects under the state directory per repository, staged uploads verified then renamed under a per-repository LFS lock

entries.question: Which LFS transfer path and storage layout does hn serve implement (FR-020, FR-021)?
entries.rationale: hn serve does not run an HTTP listener (C-002, HN-001), and git-lfs 3.x prefers git-lfs-transfer over SSH (3.7.1 is installed on the test host). Keeping LFS state outside the bare repository keeps git gc and the push check independent of LFS. Verify-then-rename under a lock ensures interrupted or mismatched uploads are never downloadable and never counted (FR-020, FR-021, the interrupted-upload edge case).

entries.final_answer: Tests build the hn binary once per test (existing buildOperationalBinary pattern) and generate one POSIX sh shim per client key. The shim reads the server home's authorized_keys, finds the managed entry whose key matches its configured public key, extracts the command= value and runs it under env -i with HOME, PATH, SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND and, when set, GIT_PROTOCOL. git, git lfs and hn reach it through GIT_SSH_COMMAND. A shim configured with an unregistered key finds no entry and fails as sshd would. One test starts /usr/sbin/sshd as the test user on a loopback port with a temporary host key; it calls t.Skip with the reason when sshd or ssh-keygen is missing or cannot start.
options: Generated shell shim used as GIT_SSH_COMMAND that looks up the generated authorized_keys entry for its key and runs that exact forced command with SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND, plus one real unprivileged sshd test skipped with a reason when unavailable

entries.question: How do acceptance tests reach the server through the forced command (C-009, OQ-9)?
entries.rationale: Running the exact command string from the generated entry tests FR-004 and FR-005 end to end without root or a system sshd. env -i reproduces the minimal sshd session environment and proves the wrapper does not rely on inherited variables. The real-sshd test covers restrict and forced-command semantics that a shim cannot prove.

entries.final_answer: Accepted grammar: COMMAND SP QUOTED-PATH [SP (upload|download)] where COMMAND is git-upload-pack, git-receive-pack, git upload-pack, git receive-pack or git-lfs-transfer (the operation argument only for git-lfs-transfer). QUOTED-PATH is an optionally single-quoted, optionally leading-slash, single segment matching [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99} with an optional .git suffix, never .. and never a symlink, and it must be registered in server state. Anything else is refused with unsupported-command or unhosted-repository before git starts. The wrapper runs git directly (no shell) with an environment built from scratch: PATH, HOME, LANG=C, GIT_PROTOCOL only when it matches version=[0-9], HN_SERVE_ACTOR, HN_SERVE_KEY, HN_SERVE_REPOSITORY. Configuration such as core.hooksPath and receive.advertisePushOptions is passed with -c flags. Every hn serve subcommand refuses to run as uid 0.
options: Strict grammar for git-upload-pack, git-receive-pack, git upload-pack, git receive-pack and git-lfs-transfer with one single-segment repository name; clean allowlisted environment; HN_SERVE_* set only by the wrapper

Other
entries.question: How does hn serve git parse SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND and build the environment for git and hooks (FR-005, NFR-003, NFR-004)?
entries.rationale: A closed grammar with no shell removes metacharacter and argument-injection classes listed in the edge cases. Rebuilding the environment means a client-sent variable cannot forge the mapped actor that hooks read. Passing configuration with -c means a hosted repository's own config cannot disable the hooks.
